description:
Tracker for implementation of the JMAP Object Metadata extension (`draft-ietf-jmap-metadata`, currently draft-01 by De Gennaro / Stalwart, expires June 2026) as a new `jmap-metadata-*` crate family.

## Why this epic exists

The workspace extras-preservation policy (JMAP-lbdy) decided 2026-05-10 to exclude filter and comparator algebra over vendor extras (see JMAP-lbdy "Decision: filter algebra excluded" and JMAP-9wh7 for the rationale and documentation propagation). The rationale: the base JMAP spec has no metaprotocol mechanism for a server to declare what extras it supports or whether they can be filtered, so silent-drop of unknown filter clauses is a query-correctness hazard.

`draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01` is the IETF-track answer to exactly that gap. It defines:

- A new capability URI: `urn:ietf:params:jmap:metadata`
- A `Metadata` object type with three flavours: `Annotation` (general-purpose vendor metadata), `ImapMetadata` (IMAP RFC 5464 mapping), `WebDavMetadata` (WebDAV dead properties)
- Annotation explicitly supports vendor-specific extension properties under a server-declared schema
- Capability declares: `dataTypes` (which JMAP types can have metadata), `metadataTypes` (which annotation `@type` values are supported), `maxDepth` (nesting depth for vendor-defined nested properties), `maySetPrivate` (per-user private metadata)
- `Metadata/query` with a `FilterCondition` (§3.4.1): `@type`, `relatedType`, `relatedId`/`relatedIds`, `isPrivate`, and crucially `textMatch` ("Only Metadata objects whose vendor-specific string properties contain the specified text are returned")
- Sortable on `id`, `@type`, `relatedType`, `relatedId`, `isPrivate`

Implementing this gives the workspace a standardised, capability-discoverable, filterable mechanism for vendor extras — solving the problem that motivated the extras filter-algebra exclusion.

## Scope (anticipated — finalise when draft stabilises)

| Crate | Role |
|---|---|
| `jmap-metadata-types` | Data types: `Metadata` enum (Annotation / ImapMetadata / WebDavMetadata variants), `MetadataFilterCondition`, `MetadataComparator` |
| `jmap-metadata-server` | Method handlers: `Metadata/get`, `Metadata/changes`, `Metadata/set`, `Metadata/query`, `Metadata/queryChanges`; capability registration; `MetadataBackend` trait |
| `jmap-metadata-client` | Client method bindings (mirror the pattern from sibling extension-client crates) |

Plus integration updates in workspace AGENTS.md (capability map table) and consumer crates (mail / calendars / contacts / tasks / filenode etc.) so they can declare which of their object types are valid `relatedType` values.

## Order of work

1. `jmap-metadata-types` — purely a sibling extension-types crate, cookie-cut from `jmap-mail-types`.
2. Capability registration in `jmap-server` (it owns the Session shape).
3. `jmap-metadata-server` — backend trait + handlers; cookie-cut from `jmap-mail-server`.
4. `jmap-metadata-client` — cookie-cut from `jmap-mail-client`.
5. Consumer-crate integration (declare which data types accept metadata).

Each stage corresponds to the established canonical-template propagation rule (workspace AGENTS.md).

## Draft-version risk

`draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01` is a real IETF Working Group document (not a vendor draft). It's an active draft, so the wire format may evolve. Mitigation: implement against -01, track the WG mailing list and rev when the draft revs. The Rust crates use `#[non_exhaustive]` everywhere so adding fields when the draft revs is non-breaking. Major wire-shape changes between revisions will require coordinated updates.

## Coordination with existing epics

- **JMAP-lbdy** (extras-preservation policy): orthogonal. Extras policy covers data-object inline round-trip; this epic covers companion-object discoverable + filterable extras. The two patterns coexist: use `extra` flatten field for opaque round-trip of unknown wire fields; use Metadata/Annotation when vendor wants the field to be queryable AND capability-declared.
- **JMAP-9wh7** (filter-algebra exclusion documentation): rustdoc and READMEs across the type crates point at this epic as the IETF-track future hook. When this epic lands, those rustdoc/README references should be updated to point at concrete crate types instead of the draft URL.

## Acceptance criteria

- New `jmap-metadata-types` crate with full Metadata/Annotation/ImapMetadata/WebDavMetadata types and their FilterCondition/Comparator.
- Round-trip tests against the draft's example JSON (with explicit "draft-NN" version pinning in test names so revs can be tracked).
- `Metadata/*` method handlers wired through `jmap-metadata-server` against a new `MetadataBackend` trait.
- Capability URI registered in `jmap-server` Session capabilities map.
- Documentation updates: workspace AGENTS.md crate map; each consumer-crate AGENTS.md notes that Metadata can attach to its types; rustdoc and READMEs from JMAP-9wh7 updated to point at the implemented crates.
- `cargo test --workspace` clean, `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean.

## Notes

- `draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01` is a real IETF Working Group document, not a vendor draft. It's the right standard to implement.
- The `textMatch` filter operation is coarse (substring search across vendor string properties), but it's a real standardised filter — better than nothing, and the spec leaves room for future extensions.
notes: De-labeling human (2026-05-11, Mark): umbrella epic for the jmap-metadata-* crate family. All implementation children are filed and most are closed. The only remaining open work (JMAP-06zp.3.5 + its decomposition into .5.1/.5.2) carries its own labels. No decision pending at the epic level.
title: EPIC: implement draft-ietf-jmap-metadata as new jmap-metadata-* crate family
